Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants using speaker equipment are advised to use handset mode for optimal sound quality. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Renewables' results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. Apex Renewables delivered a solid performance in the Q3 2024, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter:

1. First, our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm thrilled to share what has been a transformative quarter for Apex Renewables. As a leader in integrated renewable energy and clean tech solutions—spanning utility-scale solar, onshore wind, long-duration energy storage, and green hydrogen—we delivered exceptional results that underscore our execution strength amid a rapidly evolving global energy transition. We significantly outperformed our guidance, driven by robust demand from hyperscale data centers, favorable policy tailwinds like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and Europe's REPowerEU initiative, and our proprietary advancements in next-gen technologies.

Total revenue reached $1.45 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% above the high end of our guidance range. This marks our ninth straight quarter of accelerating growth, fueled by a record $6.2 billion project backlog—up 45% from Q3 2023—with 70% contracted under long-term power purchase agreements at average pricing of $45/MWh, well above our blended LCOE of $28/MWh. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $425 million, a 38% increase, expanding margins to 29.3% from 25.1% last year, thanks to scale efficiencies, lower balance-of-plant costs, and optimized operations and maintenance leveraging our AI-driven predictive analytics platform.

On the bottom line, diluted EPS was $1.12, up 42% YoY and beating consensus by 15%, reflecting not only revenue momentum but also disciplined cost management—we reduced capex per MW by 18% through vertical integration in our U.S. module manufacturing facility in Texas, now producing 5 GW annually of high-efficiency TOPCon bifacial panels at 23.5% module efficiency. Free cash flow generation was stellar at $320 million, enabling $150 million in shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks, while we maintained a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of just 1.8x.

Operationally, we commissioned 2.8 GWdc of new capacity across our portfolio, bringing our total operating assets to 12.5 GW—up 25% YoY. Highlights include the full ready-to-close of our 850 MW Gemini Solar + Storage project in Nevada, co-located with 400 MWh of our ApexFlow BESS using LFP chemistry for 4-hour duration. This project achieved a capacity factor exceeding 32% in its first month, powered by our tracker tech with 60° passive stow, and is already supplying firm, dispatchable clean power to Google under a 15-year PPA—capitalizing on the surging AI data center load growth, which now represents 25% of our U.S. pipeline.

In wind, we advanced our 500 MW onshore portfolio in the U.S. Midwest with our next-gen 5.5 MW turbines featuring 150-meter rotors and integrated recyclable blades, achieving a 48% capacity factor in initial operations—competitive with offshore benchmarks. Our clean tech segment, which grew 55% to $280 million in revenue, saw breakthroughs in green hydrogen: we energized our 100 MW PEM electrolyzer facility in Texas, producing 10,000 tonnes of H2 annually at under $2/kg, under offtake with Air Products, positioning us ahead of peers.

Regionally, North America remains our growth engine, contributing 65% of revenue with 1.9 GW added—bolstered by $1.2 billion in IRA tax credits captured this quarter, including ITC adders for domestic content and energy communities for hydrogen. Europe delivered 15% of revenue with 600 MW commissioned in Spain and Italy, navigating grid queue challenges via our 500/34 kV HVDC interconnection tech, in line with REPowerEU's 320 GW solar target by 2030. In APAC, we broke ground on a 1.2 GW hybrid solar-wind-storage project in India under the PM Surya Ghar scheme, tapping into 50 GW of annual tendering, while Australia saw our 300 MWh BESS portfolio achieve 95% roundtrip efficiency. Emerging markets like Chile and Saudi Arabia added $150 million in EPC wins, with NEOM's green hydrogen ambitions driving our MOU for 1 GW of electrolyzers.

Strategically, these results reflect our Build-Own-Operate-Stack model, where we retain 40% merchant exposure in high-value markets like ERCOT and CAISO, hedging via our proprietary ApexStack software for dynamic revenue optimization—yielding 15% uplift in capture prices. We've derisked supply chains by localizing 80% of BoP sourcing post-2023 polysilicon volatility, with panel costs down 22% to $0.22/W. Key milestones include our acquisition of BatteryTech Innovations for $450 million, accelerating solid-state battery R&D targeting 800 Wh/kg densities by 2026, and partnerships with Siemens Gamesa for hybrid wind-solar towers and Tesla for Megapack integration. Sustainability-wise, we reduced Scope 1 and 2 emissions to near-zero via 100% renewable-powered sites, and our portfolio avoided 18 million metric tons of CO2e this year—verified under SBTi. Looking ahead, we're raising full-year 2024 guidance: revenue to $5.6-5.8 billion, EBITDA to $1.55-1.60 billion, and 2025 backlog conversion targeting 4 GW deployments.

2. Next, capital recycling and asset sale transactions. Diving into one of our core value creation levers, capital recycling through strategic asset sales. In the renewable energy sector, we develop, stabilize, and monetize high-quality, cash-flowing assets to recycle capital back into our industry-leading greenfield pipeline. This disciplined approach is central to our strategy.

In Q3, we closed two marquee asset sale transactions totaling 850 MW of operational capacity, generating gross proceeds of $1.2 billion. This included the full divestiture of our 500 MW Sun Valley Solar portfolio in California's Central Valley—fully contracted under 15-year PPAs with Silicon Valley tech giants—and a 60% stake sale in our 350 MW Blackridge Wind Farm in Texas, benefiting from the full PTC wrap under the Inflation Reduction Act. These deals were executed at blended yields of 7.8% to 8.2%, with cap rates compressing to 6.5% on the solar assets due to their inflation-linked escalators averaging 2.5% annually.

Financially, these were transformative. Post-sale net proceeds of $1.05 billion—after minor transaction costs and working capital adjustments—were allocated as follows: 40% or $420 million to accelerate near-term construction starts on 1.2 GW of battery-hybrid solar projects in the ERCOT and PJM markets; 30% or $315 million to deleverage our balance sheet, reducing net debt to EBITDA from 3.8x to 3.4x; and the remaining 30% to our development war chest, bolstering our 15 GW global origination pipeline. Importantly, these sales delivered realized IRRs of 12-14% on invested capital, well above our 10% hurdle rate, and boosted our NAV per share by approximately 8% when adjusted for recycling efficiency.

Zooming out, we're seeing robust demand from infrastructure investors amid the energy transition. Global renewables M&A volumes hit $75 billion in the first nine months of 2024—up 25% year-over-year—driven by yield-hungry funds chasing stabilized assets with merchant upside or long-duration offtakes, particularly those co-located with BESS for enhanced dispatchability. In our deals, we achieved EBITDA multiples of 13.5x to 15x, a 10-15% premium to H1 averages, thanks to embedded value from our proprietary Aurora forecasting software, which optimizes merchant revenues in CAISO by dynamically stacking energy arbitrage, ancillary services, and capacity payments.

The U.S. remains our recycling powerhouse, accounting for 70% of our Q3 sales. The IRA's transferability provisions unlocked $250 million in monetized tax credits across these portfolios, supercharging after-tax yields and attracting non-traditional buyers like pension funds. In Europe, we've recycled €800 million YTD from 600 MW of onshore wind in the UK and Spain, where the market is stabilizing post-REPowerEU. We've shifted focus to repowering legacy assets—upgrading 1990s-era turbines to 5-7 MW units with 60% higher AEP—yielding 9-11% IRRs while qualifying for the EU's Innovation Fund grants. Challenges persist with higher ECB rates pushing cap rates to 7%, but our Iberian assets, backed by 20-year CfDs under Spain's auction regime, traded at a 200 bps compression. Emerging markets like Australia and India are nascent but promising; we're eyeing a 200 MW bifacial PV sale in Queensland next quarter at 8.5% yields, leveraging the Safeguard Mechanism credits.

Strategically, capital recycling preserves our DNA as developers. By selling mature assets, we retain full control over our 25 GW pipeline of shovel-ready projects, including 5 GW of offshore wind hybrids off the U.S. East Coast and 3 GW of green hydrogen-enabled electrolyzer parks in the Nordics. This develop-to-sell model allows us to sidestep yieldco dilution while partnering with long-term owners who optimize O&M—our Texas wind deal includes a 10-year turbine service agreement at fixed margins. We've also embedded ESG premiums: all Q3 sales featured Scope 1&2 verified at under 10 gCO2/kWh, commanding 50-100 bps tighter pricing.

Looking forward, we target $3-4 billion in recycling proceeds for FY2025, representing 20-25% of our capex needs. This supports a 25% CAGR in FCF through 2027, with recycling efficiency—measured as new GW originated per dollar recycled—hitting 1.8x this year. Risks include interest rate volatility and supply chain snarls for HVDC transformers, but our 18-month PPA queue with hyperscalers and 2 GW BESS delivery slots position us resiliently. In short, capital recycling fuels our flywheel: sell stabilized assets, fund innovation-led growth, and repeat.

3. Third, the impact of government incentives and subsidies. These mechanisms remain a cornerstone for accelerating deployment, reducing LCOE, and bridging to full subsidy independence. For Apex Renewables, they've been instrumental in delivering $178 million in direct tax credits and grants this quarter alone—representing 22% of our adjusted EBITDA—up 15% year-over-year from enhanced utilization under the IRA and similar programs globally.

In the U.S., which accounted for 58% of our Q3 revenue, the IRA has been transformative. The 30% Investment Tax Credit base, plus adders for domestic content, energy communities, and low-income benefits, allowed us to monetize $112 million in transferable credits from our 1.2 GW solar-plus-storage portfolio additions. Our Gemini Solar project in Nevada—a 690 MW bifacial PV facility with 380 MWh of BESS—qualified for the full 50% adder stack, boosting project IRR from 9.2% to 14.7% and enabling a record-low LCOE of $28/MWh.

The Production Tax Credit safe harbor for our onshore wind farms, including the 450 MW Prairie Winds expansion in Texas, contributed another $42 million. We've front-loaded PTC elections under the IRA's elective pay provisions, improving cash flow certainty—our DSO dropped to 45 days. We're mindful of prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements; non-compliance risks have idled 5% of our EPC pipeline, but our in-house training academy has certified 1,200 workers.

IRA-driven manufacturing credits supported our Arizona thin-film module fab ramp-up to 2 GW annual capacity, with $25 million in awards subsidizing CAPEX. In Europe, representing 24% of revenue, subsidies are shifting from feed-in tariffs to auctions and grants under REPowerEU. Our 800 MW portfolio in Spain and Germany benefited from €68 million in CfD strike prices averaging €55/MWh, shielding us from negative pricing. In Italy, the FER5 auction awarded us 250 MW at a 15-year PPA with a €45/MWh floor, enhanced by the EU's Innovation Fund grant for our floating PV initiative on Lake Garda—a 50 MW pilot with HDPE pontoons and N-type TOPCon modules for 25% higher yield.

Germany's EEG surcharge reforms reduced our effective subsidy dependency to 12% of EBITDA from 18% last year, while the UK's CfD Allocation Round 6 secured 300 MW offshore wind at £44/MWh. Subsidy phase-outs are accelerating LCOE convergence—our European utility-scale solar now hits $0.022/kWh unsubsidized. In APAC, comprising 15% of revenue, India's PLI scheme provided ₹1,200 crore in disbursements for our 1.5 GW Gujarat facility, covering 70% of cell-to-module CAPEX and enabling 22% module efficiency with HJT tech.

Australia's LRET and Capacity Investment Scheme delivered AUD 120 million for our 400 MW New South Wales wind farm, with LCFS credits adding 8% to IRR via green hydrogen pilots. Indonesia's rooftop solar subsidies under JETP unlocked 150 MW commercial installs.

Overall, incentives amplified our segment-adjusted ROIC to 11.8% versus 8.2% ex-subsidies, funding R&D into perovskite tandem cells targeting 35% efficiency by 2026 and long-duration iron-air flow batteries. Subsidies now form just 18% of total project economics, down from 32% in 2021, thanks to 25% YoY CAPEX deflation. Looking ahead, policy risks like U.S. PTC/ITC step-downs post-2025 could pressure 10-15% of our pipeline, but we diversify into corporate PPAs (now 40% of backlog), REC stacking, and green bonds at 4.2% yields. We've modeled full subsidy elimination by 2030 still delivering 12% IRR via $18/MWh LCOE targets. In total, they've been a $650 million tailwind YTD, ensuring resilience.

4. Finally, our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year. As we wrap up a transformative Q3—where we delivered 28% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.45 billion and expanded our backlog—our focus remains on scaling high-efficiency solar PV manufacturing, accelerating energy storage deployments, and pioneering next-gen clean tech amid a global renewables boom projected to add 5.5 TW by 2030.

Our four core pillars: First, manufacturing scale-up and supply chain resilience, allocated 60% of FY2025 CapEx. We're doubling down on U.S.-centric production via IRA 45X credits, unlocking $450 million YTD. Our new 5 GW TOPCon fab in Phoenix will hit 92% utilization by Q1 2025, driving costs to under $0.22/W. Q4 shipments to U.S. projects surge 35% QoQ, with Europe up 40% YoY on REPowerEU, and India via Adani partnerships. CapEx: $850 million, including polysilicon deals.

Second, energy storage leadership, targeting 25% domestic share by 2026. Our ApexFlow BESS has a $2.2 billion backlog. Q4: 1.5 GWh deployments at 28% margins. Advancing vanadium flow batteries at 98.5% efficiency. FY2025: 8 GWh output, $350 million EBITDA.

Third, innovation pipeline: R&D to 8% of revenues ($180 million), on perovskite tandems at 32% efficiency and AI inverters. Acquiring a Danish perovskite stake for $120 million; H2 electrolyzers at $450/kW.

Fourth, sustainability and capital discipline: 40% to SBTi emissions cut; $300 million buybacks, 15% dividend hike.

Q4 guidance: Revenues $580-610 million (+28% YoY), EBITDA $145-155 million. FY2025: $2.4-2.6 billion revenues (+25%), $520-560 million EBITDA, $400 million FCF. Backlog $7 billion. Assumptions: stable silicon, IRA continuity; risks mitigated via hedges and FAST-41.

In summary, we're primed for growth in a $1.7 trillion market through unmatched execution.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.45 billion, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 29.3%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $650 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $285 million, or $1.12 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. In closing, I am confident that Apex Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now take questions from the telephone lines only. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of ApexFlow BESS on your project economics?

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, our ApexFlow BESS is a game-changer for project economics. In projects like Gemini Solar, the co-location boosts IRRs by 5-6 points through enhanced dispatchability and revenue stacking—energy arbitrage, ancillary services, and capacity payments. With 95% roundtrip efficiency and LFP chemistry, it drops LCOE to $28/MWh while capturing IRA adders. We've seen 15% uplift in capture prices in ERCOT, and our $2.2 billion backlog reflects hyperscaler demand for firm power. Happy to follow up offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. Grid timelines remain a key focus. For our 4 GW 2025 pipeline, we're targeting 12-18 months in the U.S. via FAST-41 designations, shaving 20% off traditional queues. In PJM and ERCOT, 1.2 GW hybrids are interconnection-complete, with energization by Q2 2025. Europe leverages HVDC tech for Spain/Italy additions in 9 months. We've de-risked with 18-month PPA queues and Fluence slots. Challenges like transformer shortages are mitigated by 80% hedged supply chains.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
